chapter_note: The chapter is largely an old, impersonal cosmological sequence of foreordination (“before …”) describing predetermined moments in the Light’s plan: Ambassador, ships, Judge, astrological fate, destroyers, and the Builder. It is lightly framed by an introductory exhortation (¶1). One paragraph (¶5) crosses from cosmic architecture into contemporaneous polemic (“sects”), indicating an editorial/institutional application graft rather than substrate teaching.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic introductory/exhortative voice (“Once again, hear…”) functioning as editorial framing rather than cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Know that before night and day were differentiated in the universe, the Third [Am]bassador was summoned. And afterwards, he was sent to this void and outer waste that he might purify the light, and separate night and day from each other.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmic chronology and function of a named aeonic being (Third Ambassador) within the salvation mechanics; cosmos→cosmos mapping (void/outer waste; separation of night/day).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.117⟩ Before the light was released and freed and ascended through this zone, the Father of Life made beautiful for it the ships of light. He constructed them so that it might be purified in them, and be sculpted and fashioned in good order.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic salvific mechanism stated as process (release/ascend/purify) with standard Manichaean hypostases (Father of Life; ships of light), without institutional address or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: [Bef]ore Sin had multiplied and had made a kingdom in the flesh, before the acquitted and the condemn[ed] were set apart from each other, the Judge [w]as sent forth and revealed. His throne was created and placed [i]n the living atmosphere, so that he would be a just Judge, so that there the righteous and the sinners would be set apart and tested and separated from each other.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic adjudication architecture (Judge, throne, living atmosphere) expressed in the same pre-temporal deterministic mode. ‘Sin’ here behaves as an active power (‘multiplied… made a kingdom’), consistent with cosmological personification rather than a later ethical exhortation.

The correspondence leaves the cosmic system and points into a historical-religious landscape (“the sects”); this reads as institutional/polemical application of cosmic Christ-language rather than the older substrate’s self-contained cosmography.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [befo]re mankind had been engendered, some were named ['rich' and] others 'poor' on earth [ ... ] upon them. ⟨p.118⟩ Before they die, they who will die are marked out by the stars and the signs of the zodiac in the sphere. They are appointed for them; in them are their births. And their root is bound up with their zodiacal signs; and they are compelled by them and brought to an equal judgement in accordance with their deeds and their sins.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Astrological-deterministic cosmology (stars, zodiac, births, compulsion) stated structurally and impersonally; the register stays within cosmic fate mechanics rather than exhortation or church discipline.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, before the universe is dissolved, [and the] entire earth, the destroyers were appointed and instructed for its dissolution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief but purely cosmic eschatological mechanism (appointed destroyers for dissolution) in the same ‘before…’ foreordination sequence.

paragraphs.core_text: And before the ne[w] aeon was [built and] made be[auti]ful and marked out, [the] Great Builder [w]as summoned, the first architect and the angels who are with him, who would build and make beautiful the new aeon.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Self-contained cosmological construction motif (new aeon; Great Builder; first architect; angels) characteristic of systematic Manichaean cosmogony, not framed as moral instruction or citation.
